newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU exports tiny quantity of wheat with tax.
newsitem.headline: EU exports tiny quantity of wheat with tax.

text.p: Grain traders have taken out licences through France to export a tiny quantity of European Union wheat -- 280 tonnes -- with a tax of 15 Ecus per tonne, French grain officials said on Friday.

The licences were taken out through the EU's daily export channel some time between May 14, when the EU introduced taxes on wheat and flour, and May 29 when the EU reduced the soft wheat export tax from 15 to five Ecus per tonne, they said.
Industry sources said the licences were likely to cover small truck loads of wheat from France to Switzerland.
There was no word on whether export taxes had also been booked through other EU member countries.

The EU imposed taxes last month to curb wheat exports until the next harvest, and sent out a fresh signal of export restraint on Thursday by deciding to halve the usual number of weekly grain meetings during July and August.

It was not immediately clear what impact this would have on the timing of export tenders for the 1997/98 season (July/June), but officials said on Thursday they would not be issued "for the time being".

Grain traders are anxious for clearance to start covering sales of wheat and other grains from the new crop, but officials have said "prudence" is important until more is known about the state of the harvest after recent damage from drought.

Analysts say crops are recovering well in northern Europe but some southern European crops may be damaged this year. However they caution that crops rebounded to a record high last year despite similar problems in the late spring of 1996.
